What Car Would You Lease But Never Buy?

CA
By Chloe Adams Car Culture & Restomod Editor • via Jalopnik Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Jalopnik Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • When getting a new car, the age-old question is always whether it's better to buy or lease .
  • Of course, the answer often comes down to the individual, their financial situation, and what sort of commitment they're looking for, but there's another important part of the equation: The car itself.
  • Official reporting verified via Jalopnik news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • CHLOE ADAMS Car Culture & Restomod Editor

Heritage Preservation vs Modern Performance

Automotive passion is increasingly defined by the synthesis of analog soul and contemporary engineering. This coverage from Jalopnik illustrates how bespoke builders, private collectors, and restomod artists are preserving the golden eras of internal combustion while adopting carbon fiber composites and precision craftsmanship.

Big Picture: Auction hammer prices and enthusiast demand indicate sustained historical appreciation for rare, analog driver's vehicles.

When getting a new car, the age-old question is always whether it's better to buy or lease . Of course, the answer often comes down to the individual, their financial situation, and what sort of commitment they're looking for, but there's another important part of the equation: The car itself. Some cars are just better to lease than they are to buy, and that idea is what brings me to today's question.

📌 The Core Development

I want to know what car you would lease, but would never consider buying. What car, for one reason or another, could you stomach making a financial commitment to for two or three years, but once that time is over, have a dealership take it back off your hands for good?

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Obviously, there are plenty of reasons why some cars are better to lease than buy. Maybe an automaker is running good lease rates on a particular model. Maybe they've got a bit of a reputation for — let's say — being around for a good time, not a long time. Maybe you've done the math, and you've realized that a certain type of car (electric) is being updated so rapidly that committing to the technology of today long-term probably isn't going to pay off five or 10 years from now, so getting into a car for two or three years just makes more sense.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

My pick is a simple one, and it checks two of the boxes I just mentioned: unreliability and a rapidly changing EV landscape. It's the Lucid Air. I absolutely adore the Air . There's an argument that it's the best sedan on sale today, perhaps even the best vehicle, regardless of body style. It's especially appealing if you opt for the quarter-million-dollar version, the Air Sapphire , but I won't be greedy with my choice. Unfortunately, the Sapphire is a bit unreliable , and there are several known bugs with the car's software that make it hard to justify such a big price tag. It does, however, also check the EV box.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

So, while it is a fantastic car now, it probably won't be in a decade's time. And why would I want to deal with the headache and heartache of having a car that is so deeply outdated — especially when it's supposed to be software-defined? I wouldn't, and neither would you. Anyway, that's enough out of me. How about you all head on down below and let your fellow Jalops know what car you would absolutely lease but would never buy? As always, cash prizes will be given out to those who explain their answers.
